title: OS2G: A High-Performance DPU Offloading Architecture for GPU-based Deep Learning with Object Storage
problem: Object storage for deep learning workloads imposes intensive CPU processing overhead and causes redundant data movements (DPU->host->GPU), consuming host resources and creating a data ingestion bottleneck that limits GPU utilization during training.
motivation: Object storage is increasingly attractive for DL due to cost-effectiveness and scalability, but naive DPU offloading of the object storage client still burdens host CPUs with data relay tasks, preventing full benefit from DPU acceleration in GPU-based DL clusters.
method: OS2G introduces a DPU offloading architecture that establishes a direct DPU-to-GPU data path, bypassing the host CPU entirely for object storage data delivery. It redesigns the object storage client to run on the DPU and exploits GPU-Direct or equivalent RDMA mechanisms to transfer data directly from the DPU's network interface into GPU memory. OS2G includes a DPU-side data processing pipeline (decompression, format conversion) to prepare DL-ready tensors before they enter GPU memory, eliminating the host CPU from the critical data path.
key_novelty: End-to-end DPU-to-GPU direct data path for object storage in DL clusters that eliminates host CPU involvement and redundant data copies from the storage ingestion pipeline.
contributions: Characterization of CPU overhead and redundant data movement costs in naive DPU offloading for object storage in DL clusters.
OS2G architecture establishing a direct DPU-to-GPU data path that bypasses host CPU for storage I/O.
DPU-side DL-oriented data processing pipeline (decompression, format conversion) that delivers GPU-ready tensors.
limitations: Not discussed; the DPU-side processing pipeline's ability to keep up with high GPU batch throughput and scaling to multi-GPU setups is not characterized.
primary_theme: DPU-to-GPU direct data path for deep learning object storage
